analysis:
Compared all supplied BASE/HEAD ClusterApprovalWatchTests.swift text and examined ClusterOwnerServingTests.swift metadata and bounded patch. Watch tests now specify excluding negotiation failures from quick-end counts (head 211–250), retrying a failing approval after one hour, immediately retrying undated legacy records, and retrying after clock rollback (256–304). Existing tests retain coordinator-list matching, local-only isolation, per-Mac artifact checks, rollback/convergence and refusal before stopping parts (127–150, 307–475). These are test expectations, not evidence that production authorization, encryption, cache isolation or billing controls changed; no concrete security regression is established here.
The ClusterOwnerServingTests.swift patch at head 68 onward expects declared models to receive public-qualification wording for pipeline and tensor-parallel families without corresponding local records, while attributing placement qualification to the coordinator. Integration must distinguish this informational declaration from actual admission and verify that current artifact/build qualification and per-connection authorization remain authoritative (A-016, A-017, T-052–T-054; model integrity T-007/T-027). Also examine ClusterApprovalCheck, ClusterApprovalFallback, ClusterSetupRecord and ClusterService changes to confirm retries still require fresh, unexpired matching approval and local artifact validation, and that negotiation-error classification cannot suppress genuine local failures indefinitely (A-018). Test expectations alone do not prove a missing control. ClusterOwnerServingTests.swift source and its complete patch are absent; its remaining changes cannot be evaluated from ranges alone. Production-path and qualification-contract questions remain for integration, not supported findings.
